title: New event detection and topic tracking in Turkish
abstract: Evaluates new-event detection and topic tracking in a news stream. Incoming documents are assessed for whether they describe a previously unseen event and, for known events, whether they belong to an existing tracked topic.
venue: Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology

admission.reason: The capability is relevant to F2, but the abstract largely repeats the new-event-detection and topic-tracking coverage already admitted through the broader TDT evaluation framework and the more focused first-story-detection paper. Its Turkish-language setting does not, from the abstract alone, add a distinct identity or uncertainty mechanism needed badly enough to consume another reading slot. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Incremental clustering and dynamic information retrieval
abstract: Studies clustering when observations arrive dynamically and clusters must be maintained as new points are inserted. The work provides foundational algorithms for incremental cluster maintenance rather than assuming a static batch assignment.
venue: Proceedings of the 29th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing

admission.reason: Topic words match F5, but the abstract only establishes generic incremental maintenance of clusters as points are inserted. It does not show identity semantics, abstention, explicit creation of a new identity versus continuation, or later merge/split correction. Generic dynamic clustering is insufficient for the project's work-matter identity problem. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: FIRLA: a Fast Incremental Record Linkage Algorithm
abstract: Presents an incremental record-linkage algorithm that updates previously established clusters when new records arrive instead of repeating full batch linkage. The work primarily emphasizes computational efficiency while retaining the underlying identity-linkage operation.

admission.reason: The abstract concerns incremental record linkage, but emphasizes computational efficiency while retaining an existing linkage operation. Stronger candidates in this set address incremental identity with relational evidence or explicit repair of earlier clustering decisions, which are more important to msgloom than avoiding batch recomputation. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Privacy preserved incremental record linkage
abstract: Develops privacy-preserving incremental record linkage for adding records to previously linked data. New records may attach to existing clusters or form new clusters when no satisfactory existing match is found, directly reflecting an incremental continue-versus-new decision.

admission.reason: The abstract does contain the useful F9 continue-versus-new-cluster decision, but privacy preservation is the paper's distinguishing contribution and the candidate set already contains stronger incremental entity-resolution work with VERIFIED identity or explicit correction mechanisms. Given scarce reading slots, the privacy-specific variant does not materially strengthen the core identity question enough. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Incremental entity resolution on rules and data
abstract: Develops incremental entity-resolution techniques for settings where either data or matching logic changes. Previously materialized resolution results are reused to update match-based, distance-based, and pair-oriented resolutions without recomputing everything from scratch.

admission.reason: The paper is relevant to F9, but the abstract centers on reusing materialized entity-resolution results when data or matching rules change. It does not, from the abstract, provide as direct a contribution to continue/new identity, contradictory-evidence repair, or stable evolving clusters as the stronger incremental entity-resolution candidates admitted here. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: An incremental graph-partitioning algorithm for entity resolution
abstract: Presents incremental graph partitioning for entity resolution when new references arrive and pairwise similarities may change. Unlike purely greedy attachment, the method can revisit previous decisions when new or contradictory evidence changes the consistency of existing clusters.

admission.reason: The abstract clearly supports F7 by revisiting prior entity-resolution decisions when new or contradictory evidence arrives, but that contribution substantially overlaps the admitted incremental multi-source entity-resolution paper, whose abstract additionally states explicit repair of erroneous clusters and reduction of insertion-order dependence. With both identities UNCHECKED, the latter is the stronger single reading-slot choice.

title: Improved suffix blocking for record linkage and entity resolution
abstract: Develops improved suffix-based blocking methods for record linkage and entity resolution and considers incremental processing after records are inserted. The approach reduces the comparison space while preserving candidates needed to update identity clusters.

admission.reason: The paper concerns F9-related infrastructure, but the abstract's contribution is suffix blocking and reduction of the comparison space. Candidate generation efficiency does not materially answer same-identity, new-identity, abstention, or correction decisions, and therefore is secondary to the project's current research gaps. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Cross-Document Event Coreference: Annotations, Experiments, and Observations
abstract: Introduces cross-document event coreference as the problem of identifying descriptions in different documents that refer to the same real-world event. It presents annotations and experiments that establish event identity across document boundaries as a distinct coreference problem.

admission.reason: The abstract establishes the foundational cross-document event-coreference problem, but that capability is already represented by several admitted modern papers with stronger evidence on dense ambiguity, broad-collection benchmarks, cross-corpus generalization, and retrieval-scale identity. Reading this additional foundational treatment is unlikely to materially strengthen the current streams enough to justify the slot. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Cross-document Event Coreference Resolution based on Cross-media Features
abstract: Addresses cross-document event coreference in multimedia news by combining textual event information with visual evidence from news video keyframes. The work tests whether cross-media evidence can help distinguish mentions of the same real-world event from other event mentions.
venue: Proceedings of the 2015 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

admission.reason: The paper performs genuine F1 event-identity resolution, but its distinguishing contribution is visual evidence from multimedia news. Msgloom's current target is email and chat communication, and the abstract does not show a transferable identity mechanism beyond adding a modality the product does not currently use. This is therefore out of scope for the present reading round. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: A Framework for Clustering Evolving Data Streams
abstract: Presents a framework for maintaining clustering information over evolving data streams using compact online summaries and later macro-clustering. It is a general streaming-clustering foundation for tracking cluster evolution, although its clusters are not inherently identity-labelled work matters.
venue: Proceedings of the 29th International Conference on Very Large Data Bases

admission.reason: The paper is a useful general foundation for F5 streaming clustering, but the abstract describes compact summaries and later macro-clustering rather than identity-labelled clusters, continue-versus-new decisions, abstention, or correction of mistaken identity assignments. Topic words match, but the capability is too generic for this project's identity problem. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Joint Entity and Event Coreference Resolution across Documents
abstract: Presents a joint model for cross-document entity and event coreference. It iteratively constructs clusters and exploits dependencies between entity and event mentions, including predicate-argument relations, so evidence about one type can improve identity decisions about the other.
venue: Proceedings of the 2012 Joint Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and Computational Natural Language Learning

admission.reason: The abstract is directly relevant to F1, but its joint cross-document entity/event clustering and predicate-argument evidence substantially overlap the admitted 2019 joint-model paper. The newer admitted paper is sufficient for this mechanism at the admission stage, so this candidate would duplicate a reading slot rather than materially broaden the stream. Identity is UNCHECKED.
